headline: Data centers to increase emissions: IEA
claim: Data centre emissions are on course to rise about 70% by 2030, with AI driving about three-quarters of the growth in data centre electricity demand.
notes: published 2026-11-20 (page date read via WebFetch). Guardian story with AFP reporting, republished by Taipei Times. Reports the IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 central-scenario projection. Forecast, not a measurement. Figures are global; the rise is tied to fossil-fuel power in the US and China.

headline: ‘Mismatch in timing’: Data center power demand is growing 19% a year. The grid is growing 2%
claim: AI data centers raise wholesale electricity prices and shift grid costs onto existing customers, especially lower-income and rural households.
notes: published 2026-11-22 11:34 ET (page date read via WebFetch). Cites a Cornell study (Nature Energy, published 2026-11-09) finding data centers pushed up wholesale prices, by nearly 20% in parts of the Bay Area and about 17% near Dallas-Fort Worth in 2025, and covered only 38% of grid costs tied to their growth. Growth rates (19% a year, grid 2%) come from a Howden analysis, cited via an insurance broker. Article links strained supply and household costs; it reports no direct physical harm from grid strain.
